<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="79.176.221.29" /></noinclude><section begin="par119" />{{GHGmargin-letter|119|z}}
(2) On the sense of ''motion away from'' anything depends the use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} after such ideas as ''to take away from, to beware, to be afraid of, to flee, to escape, to hide oneself from'' (cf. καλύπτω ἀπό, ''custodire ab''), sometimes again in pregnant expressions, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=15}}. On the idea of ''starting from'' anything depends finally the very frequent ''causative'' use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן|translate=on account of, in consequence of}} (cf. our ''that comes from''...), ''prae'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֵרֹב|translate=for multitude}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=5}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|aa}}
(''e'') {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}}.<ref>Cf. Budie, ''Die hebr. Präpos''. ''ʿAl'' ({{GHGheb|text=עַל}}), Halle, 1882.</ref> The two original local meanings of this preposition are ''upon'' (ἐπί)<ref>Since the placing ''upon'' anything is an addition to it, {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} also implies ''in addition to'' something, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=9}} (31:50); 30:40, 32:12 (probably a proverbial saying=''mother and children''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=6}}. Also {{GHGheb|text=עַל|translate=notwithstanding}} is no doubt properly ''in addition to'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=7}} ''although thou knowest'', prop. ''in addition to thy knowing''.—From the original meaning ''upon'' is also derived that of ''on account of'' (prop. ''upon the ground of'') and ''in agreement with, according to'', since the pattern is regarded as the foundation ''upon'' which a thing stands or rests.</ref> and ''over'' (ὑπέρ, ''super'').

(1) From the original meaning ''upon'' is explained the use of {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} after ideas of ''commanding, commissioning'' ({{GHGheb|text=פָּקַד עַל־}}), &c., inasmuch as the command, obligation, &c., is ''laid upon'' the object. The construction is self-evident in the case of ''to lie, rest, lean, rely, press upon'' something; cf. also, for the last, such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, and especially {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=וְעָלַי}} prop. ''upon me'' would it have been, it would have been incumbent ''upon me'', &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|bb}}
(2) From the original meaning ''over'' is explained the use of {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} after ideas of ''covering, protecting, guarding'' {{GHGheb|text=כָּסָה עַל־}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּנַן עַל־}}; also the combinations {{GHGheb|text=רִחַם עַל־|translate=to have compassion upon}}..., {{GHGheb|text=חוּס עַל־}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָמַל עַל־|translate=to spare}} some one, arise from the idea of a compassionate or protective ''bending over'' something. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַם עַל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=17}} = ''to fight for'' some one, i.e. in his defence.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|cc}}
(3) Moreover {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} is used after verbs of ''standing'' and ''going'', to express a towering ''over'' some one or something, sometimes in phrases, in which the original local idea has altogether fallen into the background, and which are therefore to be rendered in English by means of other prepositions (''by, with, before, near''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=1}}, &c., ''Pharaoh... stood'' {{GHGheb|text=עַל־הַיְאֹר|translate=by the Nile}} (above the water level; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=1|verse=3}}), and so especially {{GHGheb|text=עָמַד עַל־}} in the pregnant sense ''to stand serving before'' some one (prop. ''over'' one who sits or reclines at table) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=4|verse=14}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=2}}, where {{GHGheb|text=מִמַּ֫עַל לְ}} is used for {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}}); {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַצֵּב עַל־|translate=to present oneself}} by command ''before'' some one, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=6}}, &c. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עַל־יַד}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַל־יְדֵי}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=14}}) ''near, at (on) the side'' of some one or something.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|dd}}
(4) From the original meaning ''above'' (not, as formerly explained, ''on to'' something, ''at'' something) there arise finally all the various constructions with {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} in the sense of ''towards, against''. The original idea (which in many of these constructions has become wholly unrecognizable) starts from the view that the assailant endeavours to take up his position ''over'' the person attacked, so as to reach him from above, or to ''over'' power him; cf. especially {{GHGheb|text=קוּם עַל־}} to rise up ''over'', i.e. ''against'' some one, then with a transference of<section end="par119" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
